text:
Alex K: hey security, got this email in my inbox asking to confirm next payroll run, looks legit at first glance. link goes to secure-pay[.]redwood-payments.com (screenshot attached)
Maria G: can you drop the raw headers and the link? do not click anything else. also which account did you use on the page?
Alex K: headers here: \nFrom: payroll-notify@redwood-payments.com\nReply-To: payroll-notify@redwood-payments.com\nReceived-SPF: fail (example.com: domain of sender does not designate permitted sender hosts)\nLink: https://secure-pay.redwood-payments[.]com/confirm\nI entered my company email and then an "enter company password" page — i typed my usual password. realized fast and closed.
SecBot: Automated phish-detector: URL submitted to sandbox for detonation (id=sbx-98712). Report will be posted when complete.
Maria G: ok treat as credential compromise until proven otherwise. Alex — we need you to change your password now (not reuse), and re-auth all sessions. we'll force-reset from backend too. Samir / Li can you start containment steps?
Samir R: revoking sessions for alex.k@redwood.com now via admin console. command: `okta sessions revoke --user alex.k@redwood.com --all`
Li Chen: blocking sender domain at gateway and adding IP block rule. also pushing an SPF/DKIM/DMARC check to infra: `siem alert` -> adding to watchlist.
Jamie: sandbox result in: 00:04:12. detonation summary: phishing kit with credential collection form, form posts to hxxp://35.201.12.78/collect. No known malware, but captures form fields and forwards to external webhook. headers indicate SPF fail and PTR mismatch.
Jamie: paste of sandbox snippet: ```POST /collect HTTP/1.1\nHost: 35.201.12.78\nUser-Agent: phish-kit/1.2\nContent: email=alex.k@redwood.com&password=*****\nAction: forwarded to tg://send?text=creds``` 
Maria G: thanks. next steps: 1) Force password reset for Alex (done) 2) Invalidate all tokens and API keys tied to that account 3) Check last 24h access logs for suspicious activity (especially console or billing) 4) Notify SSO provider for brute/credential attempts 5) Create user awareness note.
SecBot: Action log: {"action":"password_reset","user":"alex.k@redwood.com","by":"security-bot","ts":"1763504925"}
Li Chen: scanned Alex's laptop with EDR — no persistence, no malicious binaries. user clicked and submitted creds but no lateral activity from their workstation.
Samir R: checked logs: 2 failed attempts from 203.0.113.45 then 1 attempt from 198.51.100.22 which was blocked by SSO due to MFA policy. no successful console logins found.
Maria G: Outstanding: rotate any service tokens Alex had access to (Samir please list), run targeted search for the collector IP 35.201.12.78 in logs, file a request to infra to block at cloud provider. I'll draft an all-hands phishing awareness blurb.
Alex K: sorry everyone, thanks for quick response. will watch for spam and forward anything suspicious.
Jamie: marking thread as triage-complete -> containment. follow-up: security will send a mandatory phish-awareness microtraining to Eng in 24h.
SecBot: Ticket created: PHISH-2026-045 (priority: high) assigned to eng-security.
Maria G: closing notes: no evidence of data exfil, credentials likely harvested but blocked by MFA, still treat as compromise. post-incident: add this template to phish playbook and schedule a short retro.
Alex K: got it. :thumbsup:
